new_public_evidence.source: Shin, Ramdas & Rinaldo, E-detectors: A Nonparametric Framework for Sequential Change Detection
new_public_evidence.result: The e-detector framework explicitly sums start-specific e-processes. Its PFA remark states that if start weights sum to at most one, corresponding SR/CUSUM-style procedures control probability of ever false alarming, with the price that delay generally grows logarithmically with changepoint time. This directly supports a heavy-tail weighted delayed-start design.

new_public_evidence.source: Grunwald, de Heide & Koolen (2024), Safe testing
new_public_evidence.result: Conditional e-values multiply into test supermartingales/e-processes; Ville thresholding yields anytime type-I control under optional continuation. This is the type-I backbone for fixed-reference conditional block factors.

new_public_evidence.source: Brown, Durbin & Evans (1975), Techniques for Testing the Constancy of Regression Relationships Over Time
new_public_evidence.result: Classical recursive/orthogonal Gaussian residuals remove fitted mean structure while retaining constant-variance residual information. The new construction uses the simpler exact within-block centered-SSE chi-square law but follows the same orthogonal-residual idea.

derived_results.claim: The r81 Gaussian variance p-to-e channel can be replaced by direct likelihood e-factors derived from the exact reference variance confidence set. For an 8-sample future block with centered SSE W and d=7, e_up=a^{-d}exp((1-a^{-2})W/(2U^2)) is a conditional e-value for every no-change sigma0<=U when a>1; e_down with L and a<1 is a conditional e-value for every sigma0>=L. Exact chi-square mgfs prove E[e]<=1, and monotonicity makes the branch boundary the worst post-change power point.

Because the direct block factor is common to every candidate start, the infinite PFA-weighted start mixture collapses exactly to one scalar recursion per direction: A_k=e_k(A_{k-1}+pi_k), M_k=A_k+T_k, where pi_k=log2(1/log(k+1)-1/log(k+2)) and T_k=log2/log(k+2). This keeps the heavy-tail late-start penalty but removes the O(number-of-starts) state cost.
derived_results.scope: Fixed deterministic block grid; unstarted components retain unit wealth. The start weights telescope to one.

derived_results.claim: Using all d=m-1 centered Gaussian residual degrees of freedom in an m=8 block materially improves exact high-probability raw delay over the r81 disjoint-pair channel while confining an arbitrary changepoint to at most one mixed block.
derived_results.formula: For n clean post blocks and component threshold b_j, S_n=-nd log a +(a^2-1)chi2_{nd}/2. The exact chi-square lower/upper tail gives the stated 95% bounds; numeric CDF evaluations are not interval certified.

derived_results.claim: A four-direction fixed-reference block portfolio gives a complete PFA-safe guard for every fixed iid Gaussian step alternative with KL>=1 under two reference-good events. Variance ratios r<0.065 or r>3.4 go to the two block-SSE likelihood channels. For r in [0.065,3.4], KL>=1 forces |Delta|/sigma0>=sqrt(3+log(0.065)-0.065)=0.4490345..., hence |Delta|/U>=0.3905597... on the variance event. A 99% reference mean event and M_U/M_L=Xbar +/- zU/sqrt(684) leave an effective signed shift g>=0.1935811 U.
derived_results.typeI: Use mean blocks m=32 with factors exp(+/-lambda normalized_mean -lambda^2/(2m)); under no change their conditional expectation is <=1. Give all four directional e-processes equal 1/4 weight and total conditional alpha=0.03; union with variance-reference failure 0.01 and mean-reference failure 0.01 yields unconditional PFA<=0.05.
derived_results.note: These mean-delay constants are intentionally conservative: they combine worst reference-mean overshoot with worst r=3.4 alternative variance.

derived_results.claim: The r77 terminal t/F sentinel remains complementary rather than superseded. Its first-start all-KL>=1 miss upper bound was <=0.07117 after a maximum 16-sample alignment gap plus 48 clean post samples. The new block portfolio instead supplies nonshrinking late-start PFA-safe coverage with O(1) state; the early sentinel can still win on short first-start latency.

negative_or_scope_evidence: A single fixed likelihood process launched at monitoring time is not a late-change solution because its wealth can decay during a long no-change prefix. Delayed-start mixing is required; the new gain is that common block increments make the entire heavy-tail mixture recursively compressible.

The full guard is Gaussian-parametric. It assumes a clean iid pre-change reference and one fixed iid Gaussian post-change law. No heavy-tail, gradual-drift, serial-dependence or repeated-change guarantee follows.
The mean-direction certificate pays a worst-case reference-mean confidence overshoot and is much looser than the variance-direction certificate; a safe two-sample/t-style e-value may improve it.
The 95% delay integers and reference quantile ratios are float64/scipy evaluations of exact formulas, not machine-verified directed-rounding bounds.
The r81 p-to-e approach remains relevant outside parametric families; this result only dominates it for the exact Gaussian confidence-set scope.

candidate_new.mechanism: Use a fixed clean Gaussian reference to form high-probability mean/variance bounds. Monitor deterministic local blocks with four nuisance-robust conditional e-factors: two direct variance likelihood factors on centered SSE and two signed block-mean exponential factors. Mix all possible block changepoints using a telescoping heavy-tail prior whose infinite delayed-start mixture has a one-scalar recursion per direction. Keep the r77 fixed-time t/F sentinel as an early high-power companion.

Optimize block sizes and direction weights under a minimax objective over changepoint time and KL direction. Do not adopt a tuning that destroys common increments across starts, because that would lose the O(1) start-mixture recursion.
